contract: Python module exports BM25, Corpus, tokenize and LuceneTokenizer. Corpus(tokenized_documents, ids=corpus_ids); BM25(corpus).rank(query_tokens, top_k=100) returns paired unique integer document indices and finite scores in descending order.
notes: Full original corpus and all original test queries; sample_queries=0, warmup_queries=0.
Raw objective is 0.8*Recall@100 + 0.2*binary-nDCG@10 using positive qrels; this is not standard graded BEIR nDCG.
Search and confirmation use the same test queries: exploratory search-on-test, not held-out generalization evidence.
Candidate runs in a separate subprocess; grader never imports candidate code and loads qrels after candidate exit. Same UID/container does not guarantee adversarial qrels secrecy.
Pinned freeform seed uses the original pure-Python tokenizer. Java21/Pyserini belong to a separate baseline path, not this evaluator.
Prepared data manifest must be reviewed and hash-pinned in dataset-lock.json; unavailable data never becomes a fabricated score.
No published score or old evaluator baseline is inherited by this adapted protocol.
protocol_description: Pinned lexical candidate interface and byte-preserved binary metrics, with strict ranking validation and separate subprocess grading. Full prepared data required; no paper reproduction claimed.

science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
science_relevance.reason: No qualifying paper whose main objective is this underlying scientific or real-world problem has been established in the evidence registry. A task's use in an agent/framework evaluation is insufficient. This label describes the available evidence, not proof that the task has no scientific value.
